numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Numba's jitted Generator.binomial(301, 0.1, 3) returns [33, 31, 23] while the pure-Python py_func path returns [32, 31, 22] with the same seeded generators (default_rng(0)); for mid-range n the values are incorrect, and for large n the function can execute an infinite loop because a fall-through branch was not entered correctly.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Numba should replicate NumPy's C implementation of binomial, i.e. return the same values as NumPy (for the example, [32, 31, 22] as produced by the py_func/NumPy-matching path), and should not enter an infinite loop for large n.
trigger_conditions: Calling Generator.binomial with intermediate/mid-range n (example n=301, p=0.1, size=3) under numba jit
Large n with specific circumstances causing the missing fall-through to loop forever (infinite loop, a hang)
Variable p1 in random_binomial_btpe was incorrectly cast to int, which must be removed to match NumPy's distributions.c

input_output_examples.input: gen.binomial(301, 0.1, 3) with gen = np.random.default_rng(0), jitted via @jit, compared against foo.py_func(default_rng(0))

oracle_clues: Comparison of jitted output against the py_func / NumPy output for identically seeded generators
Upstream NumPy reference: numpy/random/src/distributions/distributions.c (fallthrough near lines 752-754 and binomial near line 635)
Fix described as removing int cast on p1 so it reads p1 = np.floor(2.195 * np.sqrt(n * r * q) - 4.6 * q) + 0.5

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: n=301 (intermediate/mid-range n) and n=700 (large n) for Generator.binomial; example call binomial(301, 0.1, 3) gives [33, 31, 23] under Numba vs [32, 31, 22] under NumPy
category_specific_evidence: Issue #9734: gen.binomial(301, 0.1, 3) with default_rng(0) gives [33, 31, 23] under @jit but [32, 31, 22] via py_func (NumPy); described as invalid values for intermediate-sized n
Issue #9493: with n=700 the method enters an infinite loop; for very small N=10 output matches NumPy exactly; for intermediate N=301 results are similar but deviate from NumPy
Fix diff changes p1 in random_binomial_btpe from int(np.floor(2.195*sqrt(n*r*q) - 4.6*q) + 0.5) to np.floor(2.195*sqrt(n*r*q) - 4.6*q) + 0.5, removing the int cast to mirror NumPy's C code
Fallthrough fix adds 'case = 60; continue' after the case=10 branch in random_binomial_btpe, corresponding to NumPy distributions.c fallthrough around lines 752-754
PR #9747 states the two bugs: a missing fall-through branch that together with the int-cast issue produced an infinite loop, and an incorrectly int-cast variable causing wrong mid-range values
Release note describes a numerical error fix plus an infinite loop fix in numpy.random.Generator.binomial
Added test test_binomial_specific_issues compares Numba output to py_func output with assertPreciseEqual using default_rng(0) for binomial(700, 0.1, 100) and a mid-range case with n=301
reproduction_risks: Reproduction depends on the specific generator state from default_rng(0); other seeds may not trigger the mid-range deviation or the hang
The infinite loop case (n=700) may hang rather than fail, so a reproduction needs a timeout or a check on termination
Comparison is against the Python-level py_func, and the passages give no NumPy version used for the reference outputs
Passages do not state dtype or float precision of the probability argument p; the examples only show integer outputs
